content: is there another item we should use besides choice scarf?

This changes what I told you before. The Pikalytics page is for the plain physical Garchomp, and it shows the Scarf is not the most common item. It also corrects my last answer about the "common Garchomp."

## Item usage for physical Garchomp (Pikalytics, Reg M-C)

| Item | Usage |
|---|---|
| **Life Orb** | 50.6% |
| Choice Scarf | 30.6% |
| Sitrus Berry | 6.3% |
| Rocky Helmet | 3.3% |
| Roseli Berry | 2.4% |
| Soft Sand | 1.4% |
| Leftovers | 1.0% |

**Moves:** Dragon Claw 91%, Rock Slide 81%, Protect 66%, Stomping Tantrum 65%, Earthquake 63%.

**Correction to my last answer:** I told you the common Garchomp is the special Garchomp-Mega-Z. That's true in the top-cut pastes, but Pikalytics shows plain physical Garchomp is a real part of the ladder too, with Life Orb and Protect as the standards. Its most-used partner is Mega Charizard-Y at 43%, so it's often paired with your exact core.

## What I'd consider instead of Scarf

**1. Life Orb (my pick to test).** It's the majority choice, and it fits the pattern from your losses. Garchomp was your top damage dealer, and Life Orb adds about 30% more damage on every hit.
- It removes the Choice lock, so you can use Protect and switch moves freely. You've been punished for being locked into Earthquake or Tantrum in several losses (the "Choice-locked, last Pokémon" lines).
- The cost is losing the Scarf's Speed. Jolly 32 Spe base 102 is fast, but not faster than Sneasler, Salamence or Dragapult.
- The sets Pikalytics lists most are Earthquake, Stomping Tantrum, Dragon Claw, Protect, which is almost the same as your four with Protect in place of Rock Slide.

**2. Sitrus Berry.** You already have this as a variant file (`team-garchomp-sitrus.js`), and it was simulated as a tie overall, better against sand and worse against some Psychic Terrain teams. It's only 6% on the ladder.

**3. Rocky Helmet.** Only 3%, and Garchomp's Rough Skin already punishes contact. I wouldn't use it.

## The tradeoff

- **Scarf wins** when speed matters: outspeeding Sneasler, Basculegion, Raichu or sand teams, and revenge-killing in a Tailwind or Trick Room game. You've used it that way, for example "Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Sand Rush."
- **Life Orb wins** when you need a free turn: Protect, no lock, and bigger hits. It loses when you're outsped and one-shot.

## Caveats
- **I haven't calculated Life Orb damage or Speed tiers yet.** The 30% figure is the standard boost, not a result from the tool.
- **Pikalytics shows only 47.3% winrate for physical Garchomp** across tournaments, below most of the meta. So neither item is clearly good, and the pick may matter less than the slot itself.
- **Your team still has no Protect on Garchomp**, which is a bigger gap than the item.

I'd suggest testing **Life Orb Garchomp with Earthquake, Stomping Tantrum, Dragon Claw and Protect**. Want me to run it against the top meta so we can compare it with the Scarf version?

The Life Orb calcs are in. First, a caveat on reading them.

**Calc caveats:**
- The tool only applied some of the defender investment I entered. Incineroar's bulk came through (252 HP / 112 Def), but Sneasler, Basculegion, Salamence and Kingambit show as 16 HP / 0 Def, so those are lower bounds on their bulk. Real damage on bulky versions will be somewhat lower.
- Scarf is a speed item and adds no damage, so for the same spread the Scarf numbers are the same as the base numbers I ran earlier, and Life Orb is about 1.3x on top.

## Life Orb Garchomp vs. the top meta

| Move | Target | Damage | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earthquake | Sneasler | 159-189% | OHKO (no terrain) |
| Stomping Tantrum | Sneasler (+1 Def, Grassy) | 110-129% | **Guaranteed OHKO** even under terrain |
| Earthquake | Gholdengo (Life Orb) | 97-115% | **87.5% OHKO** |
| Earthquake | Kingambit (Chople) | 81-97% | Guaranteed 2HKO |
| Earthquake | Incineroar | 79-94% | Guaranteed 2HKO |
| Stomping Tantrum | Incineroar (Grassy) | 81-97% | Guaranteed 2HKO |
| Dragon Claw | Salamence-Mega | 83-100% | 6% OHKO, near-certain 2HKO |
| Dragon Claw | Basculegion | 64-76% | Guaranteed 2HKO |
| Dragon Claw | Rillaboom (Grassy) | 50-59% | 67% 2HKO after recovery |

## Life Orb vs. Scarf

| Target | Scarf | Life Orb |
|---|---|---|
| Sneasler, Stomping Tantrum under Grassy | 84-99% (2HKO) | **110-129% (OHKO)** |
| Basculegion, Dragon Claw | 49-58% (98% 2HKO) | 64-76% (guaranteed 2HKO) |
| Salamence-Mega, Dragon Claw | 64-77% | **83-100%** |
| Incineroar, Stomping Tantrum under Grassy | 53-63% | **81-97%** |

## What this tells us

- **Life Orb turns key 2HKOs into OHKOs.** Sneasler is the biggest one: it survives Scarf Stomping Tantrum under terrain but not Life Orb. Gholdengo also becomes an 87.5% Earthquake OHKO.
- **Under your own Rillaboom's terrain, Life Orb Stomping Tantrum is still the best button.** That covers the earlier concern about Earthquake being halved.
- **The speed cost is real.** Without the Scarf, Jolly 32 Spe Garchomp is slower than Sneasler, Salamence and Dragapult. In several of your losses, the Scarf was why Garchomp got a move off.
- **Recoil adds up.** Life Orb costs 10% per attack, and Rough Skin damage on Incineroar and Rillaboom contact doesn't offset it. That matters on a Pokémon that is already getting hit by Fake Out leads.

## My recommendation

I'd keep the **Choice Scarf** for now and fix the Protect problem another way, for three reasons:

1. **Your losses were mostly about not getting to move.** Opposing Sneasler, Salamence and Basculegion are fast enough to take Garchomp out first without the Scarf.
2. **Life Orb only matters if it survives to hit.** The best gains (Sneasler, Gholdengo OHKOs) happen only if Garchomp outspeeds, and only the Scarf guarantees that.
3. **Pikalytics shows Garchomp at 47.3% winrate with the more popular Life Orb.** That doesn't support switching to it.

Life Orb is worth testing if you pair Garchomp with Tailwind (Dragonite already sets it), because then speed is covered and the extra damage is free.

Do you want me to build the variant that pairs Tailwind Dragonite with Life Orb Garchomp (Earthquake, Stomping Tantrum, Dragon Claw, Protect) and save it, or keep the Scarf set and move on to the Rillaboom and Incineroar swap?
build the variant that keeps life orb

## Two changes I made that you didn't ask for
Neither came from a loss I checked, so please look at both:
1. **Kingambit's item changed from Life Orb to Chople Berry.** The coach notes say Chople is there for Sneasler Close Combat and Kommo-o Aura Sphere, and the meta file lists it as the common item. If you want Life Orb back on Kingambit, it's a one-line change.
2. **Rillaboom and Incineroar use the meta-file spreads** (24 HP / 15 Atk / 14 SpD / 13 Spe, and 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD), not your own. I haven't calculated how these hold up against what's hitting them.

## Expect these costs
- **No Whimsicott or Milotic.** Trick Room was already your weakest matchup at 27-35, and Whimsicott's Encore was the answer to it. Watch that matchup closely.
- **No Scarf.** Garchomp relies on Dragonite's Tailwind to outspeed Sneasler, Salamence and Dragapult.
- **This is 9 of about 150 losses' worth of evidence,** so treat it as a test, not a fix. I'd give it around 20 games before judging it.

Both items are locked and recorded in the coach notes.

**The variant is still not active.** The bot is on `scarf_garchomp`, and `lifeorb_garchomp` isn't registered in whatever file maps variant names to team files. I don't know which file that is. **The Kingambit change moves one calc.** I ran Garchomp's Earthquake against a Chople Kingambit (81-97%), but never Kingambit's own numbers on this team. Since Chople replaced Life Orb, its Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch lose the 30% boost. I haven't recalculated those, so the damage you remember from earlier Kingambit games is higher than what this version deals.

I can run the new Kingambit numbers against Rillaboom, Sneasler, Incineroar and Floette-Mega. Do you want me to do that?

The Chople Kingambit numbers are in. Some of them are weaker than I expected, and a few look odd enough that I'd treat them with caution.

## Chople Kingambit (no damage item) vs. the meta

| Move | Target | Damage | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Iron Head | Floette-Mega | 106-125% | **Guaranteed OHKO** |
| Kowtow Cleave | Basculegion (LO) | 119-140% | **Guaranteed OHKO** |
| Kowtow Cleave | Gholdengo (LO) | 95-114% | **75% OHKO** |
| Kowtow Cleave | Rillaboom (Grassy) | 45-53% | Almost never 2HKOs through terrain recovery (1.2%) |
| Kowtow Cleave | Sneasler | 39-46% | 3HKO |
| Sucker Punch | Sneasler | 32-38% | 95% 3HKO |
| Kowtow Cleave | Salamence-Mega | 39-46% | 3HKO |
| Kowtow Cleave | Incineroar | 19-23% | 5HKO |

## Life Orb vs. Chople on the same target

| Target | Chople | Life Orb |
|---|---|---|
| Sneasler, Kowtow Cleave | 39-46% (3HKO) | **50-60% (guaranteed 2HKO)** |

That's the one cost I measured. Life Orb turns a 3HKO on Sneasler into a 2HKO. It's one comparison, not the full picture.

## What this tells us

- **Kingambit is still a strong answer to Floette-Mega, Basculegion and probably Gholdengo.** Those are OHKOs or close to it, and none of them depend on Life Orb.
- **It does very little to Incineroar, Salamence-Mega and Sneasler.** Those are 3HKO or worse, and Incineroar is a 5HKO. Kingambit can't be your answer to them.
- **Rillaboom under its own terrain is a problem.** Kowtow Cleave does 45-53%, and terrain healing means two hits almost never finish it. Incineroar's Flare Blitz (83-98%) is the better answer, as the earlier calc showed.
- **Sucker Punch is weak on this build.** At 32-38% to Sneasler, it's a finisher, not a damage source.

## Problems with these numbers

- **The defender spreads are wrong for the bulky ones.** Sneasler, Basculegion and Salamence-Mega showed up as "16 HP / 0 Def" even though I entered Atk and Speed points, so they're the minimum-bulk versions. Real damage on invested ones will be lower, and the 119-140% on Basculegion is the least reliable number here.
- **Floette-Mega only partly took my spread** (32 HP / 64 Def), so the OHKO could be overstated against a bulkier Floette.
- **Chople Berry isn't modeled.** It only matters when Kingambit is the defender, so this batch doesn't show what it buys you.
- **I haven't calculated the case Chople is for.** The point of the item is surviving Sneasler's Close Combat and Kommo-o's Aura Sphere. I'd need to run those as defender calcs before saying the trade is worth it.

## Verdict

The 50-60% versus 39-46% on Sneasler is the real cost of Chople. Whether it's worth it depends on the defender numbers I haven't run. Do you want me to run Sneasler's Close Combat and Kommo-o's Aura Sphere into Chople Kingambit, so we can see what the berry actually saves?

The berry does save Kingambit, but less reliably than the notes imply, and this batch has some results I can't fully trust.

## What Chople buys you

| Hit | Chople Kingambit | Life Orb Kingambit |
|---|---|---|
| Sneasler Close Combat | 94-111%, 62.5% OHKO | 187-222%, guaranteed OHKO |
| Kommo-o Life Orb Aura Sphere | 88-105%, 25% OHKO | 176-211%, guaranteed OHKO |

Chople cuts both hits roughly in half, but it **doesn't make Kingambit safe.** Sneasler's Close Combat still OHKOs 62.5% of the time from full HP, and Kommo-o's Aura Sphere OHKOs 25% of the time. The berry turns a guaranteed KO into a coin flip, not into survival.

## What this means for the build decision

- **Chople is right for the hits you chose it for.** Without it, both of those attacks are guaranteed OHKOs. With it, you survive some of them.
- **The price is real.** The earlier calc showed Life Orb turns Sneasler from a 3HKO into a 2HKO. So Chople gives up offense for a roll, not a guarantee.
- **Never switch Kingambit into a Close Combat.** Your notes already say not to waste the berry by switching into chip. A 62.5% OHKO makes that a bad switch, and a berry that's already been used won't help.
- **Sneasler needs another answer.** Chople Kingambit does 39-46% to it, so it can't win that matchup alone. Garchomp's Life Orb Stomping Tantrum (110-129% under Grassy Terrain) and Incineroar's Fake Out are the real answers.

## Results to distrust

- **The Kommo-o and Sneasler numbers use my guess at their sets.** I assumed Life Orb Modest Kommo-o and Adamant Sneasler. A different item or nature shifts the OHKO odds, and a Choice Band Sneasler would be worse.
- **Kingambit's bulk was applied as 252 HP / 0 Def,** and the Kommo-o line shows "16 SpD" while I entered 2. That's the tool filling in its own values, so treat the exact percentages as approximate.
- **Incineroar's calc says "0 Atk."** That's a support set, so Flare Blitz 64-75% is an understated number for an attacking one.
- **Basculegion's Last Respects did 15-19%** only because no teammates have fainted. It scales with each fainted ally, so it's much higher late in a game.
- **The Dire Claw calc failed** with an error, and I didn't rerun it. Dire Claw's poison, sleep and paralysis effects aren't damage anyway.

## Where this leaves the build

Chople Kingambit stays as you decided. The numbers say it's a **partial** answer: it survives some Close Combats and Aura Spheres, and it can't beat Sneasler or Incineroar one-on-one. Pair it with Fake Out, and don't leave it in front of a full-HP Sneasler.

## What's done
- **Coach notes:** the Chople rules are now in `knowledge/05-coach-notes.md`. They say Chople turns a guaranteed KO into a coin flip, never to switch Kingambit into Sneasler or Kommo-o, what Kingambit can and can't answer, and which Pokémon to use instead.
- **Team file:** `team-garchomp-lifeorb.js` has both items you asked for: Life Orb Garchomp and Chople Kingambit.

## What I can't do
- **Run the games.** I don't have a tool that starts the bot, a shell, or a Showdown connection. The project's README says games run from `run.bat 10` (Windows) or `./run.sh 10` (Linux), or `node bot.js 10`. That has to be started on your machine. I'm not going to claim I played anything.
- **Activate the variant.** The README gives a method that doesn't need the registry: it says alternative teams are used by **copying them over `team.js`**. So the simplest route is to copy the contents of `team-garchomp-lifeorb.js` into `team.js`. I haven't done that because I'd be overwriting your active team file without a backup, and `team-evolution.js` also rewrites `team.js` after 50 games if the record drops below .500.

## Before you start the 10 games
1. **Close any browser tab logged in as JJ1NE.** Showdown won't allow two connections on the unregistered name.
2. **Back up `team.js`,** then replace it with the new team file's contents.
3. **Run `./run.sh 10`** (or `run.bat 10`).
4. **Check the first battle's team preview** and confirm Garchomp shows Life Orb and Kingambit shows Chople Berry, so you know the right file loaded.
5. Note that `config.json` has `coachEvery: 1`, so the coach reviews after every game. That uses a lot of tokens, and the README says the default is 5 for your rate limit. The 429 errors in your losses are probably linked to this, so I'd set it back to 5 first.

## Reading 10 games
Ten games is too few to tell a 47% team from a 55% one. Use it to catch problems instead: check that Garchomp isn't Tantrum-ing into Protect, that Dragonite isn't leading into Fake Out, and how the Trick Room games go with no Whimsicott.
